name: Watney Robotics
summary: Watney builds autonomous robotic systems for physical operations inside data centres and supercomputing infrastructure.
overview: Watney deploys autonomous robots to help data-centre operators accelerate physical infrastructure work. In September 2026, it announced an $80 million Series A, bringing total funding above $100 million.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Watney says the financing brought total funding above $100M; valuation was not disclosed.

bull_case: Data-centre construction and operations are bottlenecked by physical work. Robots that safely raise deployment throughput can create value as AI infrastructure scales.
bear_case: Data-centre environments are safety-critical and customer qualification cycles are demanding. The company has not disclosed a valuation, commercial revenue or deployment metrics.
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

intelligence.description: Autonomous robotic systems for data-centre and supercomputing operations.
company: Watney builds and deploys autonomous robots for data-centre operations, starting with the physical work that can slow capacity expansion. The company says its systems operate alongside technicians in equipment-dense facilities and help hyperscalers build infrastructure faster.
Watney announced an $80 million Series A in September 2026, bringing total funding above $100 million. The company did not disclose a valuation.
intelligence.why_it_matters: The AI buildout needs more than chips and power: it also needs physical infrastructure assembled and maintained quickly. Watney is a private-market bet on automating that labour-intensive layer.

changed.text: Watney announced an $80M Series A led by the Valor Atreides AI Fund and Hummingbird Ventures.

takeaways: Watney builds autonomous robots for physical operations in data-centre infrastructure.
It announced an $80M Series A in September 2026, bringing total funding above $100M.
Safety, real-world uptime and hyperscaler deployment are the key execution tests.
